1.note: Jerome, Quaestiones hebraicae in Genesim (on Gen 46:27). The speaker in Acts is Stephen.

2.he: מזולת כי גם אלוה בלשון יחיד נקוד חטף סגול
2.note: The argument is compressed. He seems to offer the vocalization of Eloah as a further, non-kabbalistic explanation of the sheva under the yod.

3.note: Probably Teseo Ambrogio degli Albonesi of Pavia, Introductio in Chaldaicam linguam, Syriacam atque Armenicam et decem alias linguas (1539).

4.note: Apparently a form of פתרונו, 'its meaning'; translated in that sense.

5.note: The cited passage on the Platonic view not contradicting the Torah is in Guide II:25. The author's number is kept.

6.note: The phrase is unclear; it is taken as equivalent to כל סוף דבר, 'at any rate'.

7.note: Apparently Augustine's De civitate Dei ('his City'). The book reference is kept as given.

8.note: This echoes b. Berakhot 33b, 'he makes the attributes of the Holy One compassion (raḥamim), though they are only decrees'. המלה is understood as חמלה, 'compassion'.

9.note: The word is unclear; it is taken in the sense of בלי ערך, 'beyond compare'.

10.note: Literally 'from their bitterness'. The intended sense may be 'from their matter' (מחמרן), i.e. the body.

11.he: היוסיפון ליהודים ספר ו' פס"ג ולרומיים ספר י"ח פ"י
11.note: The author's references are kept. 'For the Romans' points to the Jewish Antiquities (the Philo embassy is at Ant. 18.8 in modern numbering). 'For the Jews' may refer to the Hebrew Yosippon or to the Jewish War.
